outcome: The app frame and API client run on API 1.24.0 data and rules
acceptance_criteria: A `/me` with positions "PMO Lead" and "Finance Lead" shows "PMO Lead, Finance Lead" beside the name on both bars. The page makes no `GET /api/v1/role-dashboard` call. — verify: `frontend/tests/shell-live.test.tsx`, fetch stub calls contain no `/role-dashboard`; the account menu header shows the names.
A `/me` with no positions shows the name only, with no stray separator. — verify: same test file.
Destinations `my_work` (available), `setup` (`available:false`) show only My work in the menu; Setup is not in the bar or the phone menu. — verify: shell test reads link names on both bars.
Each link's `href` equals the destination `url`. A `django_url` of `/retired/` and a `work_desk_url` never appear in any `href`. — verify: shell test asserts hrefs and greps rendered HTML.

A destination `url` of `https://evil.example/x`, `//evil.example`, or `javascript:alert(1)` is not rendered as a link. A same-origin absolute URL becomes its path. — verify: unit test of the url check.
All destinations unavailable shows "No sections are open to your role yet." — verify: shell test.

A keyed POST (body has `idempotency_key: "k1"`) answering 403 `csrf_failed` then 200 sends exactly: POST, `GET /api/v1/session`, POST. Both POSTs carry byte-identical bodies with `k1`; the second carries the new token from the session read; the caller gets the 200 data. — verify: `frontend/tests/client.test.ts` fetch stub call log.
Two `csrf_failed` answers in a row give an error of kind `csrf` after exactly two POSTs and one `/session` read; no third POST. — verify: client test.
A 403 with another code (`forbidden`), a 401, a 409, a 422, a 429 and a 503 on a keyed write each cause exactly one POST and no `/session` read. — verify: client test, table-driven.
A keyed write whose retry returns 409 `idempotency_conflict` or 422 surfaces that error normally. A failing `GET /session` surfaces kind `csrf` after one POST. — verify: client test.

Duplicate-effect check: a stub backend that runs the handler only on non-403 answers and counts effects for key `k1` shows one effect after a `csrf_failed` then success. — verify: client test asserts count is 1.

A write with no `idempotency_key` (sign-out `POST /api/v1/session/logout`) answering `csrf_failed` is sent once, refreshes the token once, and keeps the existing toast. — verify: `frontend/tests/sign-in.test.tsx` and client test.
A GET is never retried on `csrf_failed`. A multipart or non-JSON body write is never retried. — verify: client test.

A 429 body `{code:"rate_limited",message:"Slow down for 30 seconds."}` gives an error whose message is that text and code `rate_limited`; the same for 503 `read_limited`. A 429 with an HTML body gives the fixed fallback text. A response with no `Retry-After` header causes no error. — verify: `frontend/tests/client.test.ts`.

`download('/cases/c1/files/u1/')` answering 401 JSON throws kind `unauthenticated` and the frame main area shows "You're signed out." with a Sign in link to `/sign-in?next=...`. No redirect is followed. — verify: client test plus a shell test that triggers the notifier.
`download` answering 200 returns the blob; 403 and 404 map to `forbidden` and `not_found` and do not show the signed-out state. — verify: client test.
An admin `/me` with no `invite_minutes` anywhere renders the frame with the Admin role words. — verify: shell test.
The v7 mock path still works: with a v7 `/me` (no `url`, no `available`) the five links appear at their fixed paths. — verify: `frontend/tests/shell.test.tsx` passes unchanged.
`npm run gen:api:live` produces no diff in `src/api/live-schema.d.ts`. — verify: `git diff --exit-code frontend/src/api/live-schema.d.ts` after running it.

risk.rationale: High, because the retry lives in src/api and applies to every write in the product, including sign-in (F-58) and the money and payment features coming in later waves. A retry that mints a new key, loops, or repeats a non-csrf failure could double-execute an effect that is hard to undo. Auth and security apply because the change touches session refresh, CSRF and the signed-out state. Contract-change applies because it moves the client from v7 to 1.24.0 fields. Merge goes through the security review and a technical reviewer on the high-risk route (Opus per D-123). Per D-184, sign-in and security surfaces still come to the design engineer.
